purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and inspection program for the authoritative wasteland weigh station asset, preserving a recognizable roadside commercial-vehicle inspection site with scale lanes, bypass control, inspection functions, staff space, utilities, signage, terrain seating and coherent abandonment damage.
ground_program: highway approach visibly separates commercial-vehicle inspection traffic from through traffic, with deceleration, queue and merge geometry appropriate to heavy vehicles
primary weigh lane contains a legible scale deck or equivalent weighing platform aligned to truck wheel paths and connected to the inspection/control function
bypass lane remains distinct from the active inspection lane and reconnects to the roadway without impossible crossings or abrupt elevation changes
inspection building provides staff entrance, public or driver contact point, control/work area, records or equipment storage, sanitation and basic break space as footprint permits
secondary inspection apron or pull-off area provides room for stopped commercial vehicles without blocking the scale lane or highway merge
barriers, bollards, signs, lane markings, lighting and any gate hardware are placed to support traffic control rather than decorative clutter
electrical service, communications, drainage, heating/mechanical equipment and scale-service access are represented as maintainable infrastructure
paving, shoulders, drainage ditches, sign foundations, scale pit edges and retaining features seat the station into terrain without floating slabs, buried doors or disconnected road grades
upper_program: roof structure supports lights, antennas, vents and mechanical equipment with plausible curbs, frames or service access
any inspection canopy uses visible columns and beams and maintains adequate clearance over commercial vehicles
freestanding highway signage uses foundations and support frames appropriate to roadside wind exposure and long-distance visibility
raised observation or signal equipment, if present, has a safe maintenance route and does not substitute for occupied circulation
rooftop or elevated service equipment remains physically supported and reachable for maintenance
circulation: commercial vehicles can decelerate, queue, enter the scale lane, stop for inspection, use a secondary inspection area when required and merge back to the highway without impossible turns
through or bypass traffic remains spatially separate from queued inspection traffic wherever the site layout permits
drivers can reach the contact or inspection point without crossing uncontrolled high-speed lanes
staff circulation connects control, records, sanitation, equipment, inspection apron and exterior service points as a coherent work network
maintenance access reaches the scale mechanism, signs, lighting, communications, drainage and building utilities without blocking the only traffic lane
pedestrian routes and guardrails prevent routine movement through active truck wheel paths
equipment ladders do not substitute for architectural stairs in occupied spaces
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a weigh station through the surviving highway approach, scale lane, inspection building, signage and merge geometry
favor localized pavement failure, scale damage, vehicle impact, canopy or sign collapse, vandalism, scavenging, electrical fire and weather exposure over uniform random deletion
damage to the scale should expose or disrupt weighing infrastructure without erasing the scale-lane relationship that communicates site function
sign, canopy and roof failures must follow identifiable support loss and resolve attached fixtures so floating fragments are not left behind
building damage should preserve at least one viable exploration path through the control or inspection spaces
road connections, queue lanes, bypass lane and drainage should remain spatially coherent after damage rather than becoming disconnected slabs
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master
